# C++ actual-density profile recovery

Goal: implement and qualify current-distribution no-motion profile recovery under #391 after the supplied-profile foundation in PR #430. Preserve the corrected MATLAB default numerical contract and keep density output rows rejected until event evaluation, APV and persistence qualification are complete. MATLAB production, saved-file schemas and the v5 checkout are outside the edit scope.

The full-field entry borrows MATLAB-order density samples and vertical integration weights. An exactly horizontally uniform strictly stable field returns its profile without fitting. Otherwise, current minimum/maximum density define normalized raw moments 1 through Nz. A 4,096-sample tile bounds normalized-value and recurrence-power storage; weighted accumulation keeps the supplied quadrature normalization rather than rescaling weights to sum exactly to one.

The fit starts from the original reference profile's normalized log-gap shape and uses the corrected damped least-squares loop. A portable Householder QR solves the augmented rectangular system directly. O(Nz²) workspace is allocated before iteration, with bounded iteration/evaluation counts and explicit termination reporting. A positive solver exit alone is insufficient: publication also requires maximum normalized residual at most 1e-8 and a finite strictly decreasing physical profile at the current endpoints. Failure preserves the previous caller output.

## Verification plan and ledger

- Independent C++ weighted-moment and known parcel-permutation controls, exact stable-rest behavior, malformed-input/budget/unqualified-fit rejection, allocation failure and bounded workspace checks.
- MATLAB parity on small distributions and both retained 43/86-node JAMES moment fixtures. Compare physical profile and inverse/APE consequences separately from residual and convergence criteria; do not require identical iteration counts under different QR rounding.
- Once compact parity passes, one authoring-only full-state campaign uses each JAMES snapshot with three warmed alternating MATLAB/C++ trials for moment extraction and fitting. Record raw timing samples, input/source provenance and memory bounds; do not run concurrent timed workloads or long integrations. Retained compact fixtures stay in CI.
- Focused Release and ASan/UBSan tests, affected MATLAB methods, Code Analyzer, CI routing/artifact tests, documentation generation/comparison and repository/source-digest checks complete the handoff. Required hosted CI remains the PR integration gate.
- PR #430's first two hosted attempts failed before compilation because the runner's unused Chrome APT repository served an inconsistent package index. Prerequisite repair `57845afa` disables only the dedicated Chrome source while retaining integrity checks; its 42 CI policy tests pass. Recovery work includes that prerequisite, with hosted qualification tracked on #430.

Executed results and any failed iterations are recorded here and in `.github/ci-evidence/issue-391-density-recovery/` as qualification proceeds. Historical MATLAB receipts retain their original provenance.

## Captured-profile arithmetic assessment

The first compact MATLAB batch passed five of six methods. Both captured fits met the unchanged residual/convergence gates, but an initial 1e-8-density-range profile comparison and fixed 1 mm height comparison failed: maximum density differences were 7.326e-7 / 3.250e-7 kg m-3 and maximum height differences approximately 1.014 / 1.011 mm. No failed result or initial bound is discarded.

An independent experiment compiled the unchanged C++ solver with FMA contraction disabled. This alone changed fitted nodes by 2.240e-7 / 3.103e-7 kg m-3 while moments changed by 5.17e-13 / 1.25e-12. The normalized-density raw-moment Jacobians have numerical ranks 23/41 and 27/84 at the standard double-precision cutoff; their unresolved singular values do not support a meaningful precise condition number. Review found no QR or objective defect. MATLAB evaluation of the reconstructed C++ profile also reaches the qualified residual and gradient levels.

Based on that arithmetic sensitivity, captured-profile comparisons use explicit one-part-per-million bounds relative to the density range and depth. The solver's acceptance threshold remains 1e-8 and the stronger captured residual check remains 1e-9; analytic small-distribution tolerances, endpoints, ordering and failure gates are unchanged. Before full-state measurement, additional gates were set for mean displacement difference (1e-8 of depth), relative mean APE difference (1e-5), finite bounded material heights, nonnegative APE and density closure at rounding accuracy. Full-state measurements must pass these separately; small raw-moment residuals alone do not qualify a fit.

## Final execution results

- The new C++ target passes Release and ASan/UBSan with the final sources. Independent review corrected two real moment-normalization edge cases before final qualification: stable-rest return now precedes unnecessary normalized-weight arithmetic, and weights apply to the complete horizontal mean so subnormal contributions cannot disappear merely from tile subdivision. Regressions cover both two-sample and 32,771-sample planes. Eight independent accumulation lanes improve SIMD execution without fast-math, extra volume arrays or a changed mathematical objective; separate review confirms tail bounds and the stated vector-capacity ledger.
- All six MATLAB methods pass through focused runs: initial five passes, captured-only rerun after the documented physical-budget decision, and final four affected extraction/recovery methods after the scan changes. Test and authoring-benchmark Code Analyzer findings are zero. The original failed captured comparison, subsequent arithmetic diagnosis and scalar performance baseline remain retained.
- Three warmed alternating trials per stage on each actual JAMES state pass all prospective physical gates. Final maximum material-height differences are 0.647 / 0.834 mm; volume-mean displacement differences are 2.618e-5 / 1.506e-5 m; relative mean APE differences are 1.361e-8 / 1.610e-9. Stored-double density closure is zero and neither implementation produces negative APE. These isolate recovery with the same MATLAB profile calculus, whose C++ equivalent was independently qualified in #430.
- Final MATLAB/C++ moment medians are 0.0280/0.0208 s and 0.3593/0.3041 s, giving 1.35x/1.18x speedups. The initial scalar C++ scan took 0.0721/1.1189 s; all initial samples and hashes are preserved. Final same-target fit medians are 0.0240/0.0132 s and 0.0953/0.1026 s: the larger C++ fit is about 7.7% slower. No complete-model or whole-pipeline speedup is claimed. Peak recovery vector capacity is 67,256 / 238,672 bytes, excluding the borrowed volume, caller output and object/allocator metadata; this is not RSS.
- All 42 CI policy tests pass, including permanent MATLAB/sanitizer selection and probe artifact registration. Documentation generation and comparison pass with 2,026 files / 4,145 routes and zero differences; generated changes are limited to version history. Final source hashes, JSON, whitespace, package-manifest and repository-scope checks complete the handoff; no MATLAB production, released snapshot or v5 file is edited.
- The repaired #430 CI then exposed an undeclared `range` toolbox dependency in its new MATLAB test. Prerequisite `275c553f` replaces both calls with equivalent base-MATLAB max-minus-min expressions without changing tolerances. All four affected methods and Code Analyzer pass; original foundation receipts retain their original test hashes, with the correction explicitly recorded. #430 is armed to merge only after required hosted checks pass.

The catalog remains 76 identities / 666 rows, with 634 implemented and all 32 density rows intentionally incompatible. Next, integrate shared per-event density/profile/displacement/APE evaluation, then APV and complete output/restart/persistence qualification before promoting those rows. This goal ends with a reviewable recovery PR and issue updates; it does not claim full density output support.
